what_this_is: The author's blind page-type labelling of 40 pages that answered 2xx, scored against the destination regex the dereference audit used. This is what decides whether a corrected corpus-level estimate can be restored or whether the rule's error rate must be reported as a limitation.

provenance.what_the_two_hashes_are: blank = the sheet as issued, proving the items were frozen before any label; filled = the bytes actually scored, identifying THIS grading.
provenance.graded_by: the author, blind to the audit's classification of every item

headline.what_this_sheet_measures: The INSTRUMENT, not the corpus. The regex's precision and recall below are the result. The shares are descriptive of the probed pages only -- see the denominator warning.

share_that_is_a_document_page_WEIGHTED_T.projection_carries_no_joint_coverage: Per-stratum Clopper-Pearson bounds combined under population weights. NOT a simultaneous interval and NOT a confidence interval for the weighted total.

share_the_regex_cannot_see_WEIGHTED_TO_T.projection_carries_no_joint_coverage: Per-stratum Clopper-Pearson bounds combined under population weights. NOT a simultaneous interval and NOT a confidence interval for the weighted total.

headline.DENOMINATOR_WARNING: Those two shares are weighted by each stratum's share of the 2xx PROBE POOL, not of the corpus. The issue stratum is 33.7 % of the pool and 0.87 % of the 16,478 distinct URLs, because it was deliberately censused -- it is over-represented about thirty-ninefold. Reading either share as a corpus figure is the same error as reading the relevance sheet's naive 2/40 as a rate. Neither is quoted in the paper.

share_that_is_a_document_page_WEIGHTED_T.projection_carries_no_joint_coverage: Per-stratum Clopper-Pearson bounds combined under population weights. NOT a simultaneous interval and NOT a confidence interval for the weighted total.

headline.population_weighted_still_conditions_on_: Even this one is the share among pages that ANSWERED. The population's 2xx composition is not known exactly, because reachability differs by stratum, so it is an approximation and is not quoted in the paper either.

the_regex_under_test.rule: final URL matched /issue/(view|archive)/ -> index; anything else -> not an index

post_stratified.projection_carries_no_joint_coverage: Per-stratum Clopper-Pearson bounds combined under population weights. NOT a simultaneous interval and NOT a confidence interval for the weighted total.

precision_of_not_an_index.reading: Of the pages the rule passed as 'not an index', how many are really a single document page. Anything below 1.00 means quantity 3a over-counted.

recall_on_indexes.reading: Of the pages a person calls an index, how many the rule caught. The regex knows one URL shape, so an index served at any other path is invisible.

is_it_the_cited_document.note: 'stored_title_unusable' is a CORPUS defect, not a destination failure, and is counted apart. Scoring it as 'different_document' would blame the destination for an ingestion bug.
